title: The Compiler already lowers the SoL-ExecBench FP16 GEMM shape to CUDA on sm_103a; three layers above it refuse FP16, and the Triton route declares no FP16 dot

evidence.note: This finding has no campaign evidence and claims no measurement. It is a set of Compiler.assess probes over corpus schedules, each reproducible from the checkout at the cited Compiler Revision. No device was used and no latency is reported.

Retyping every bf16 buffer to fp16, dropping the bias chain and narrowing the FP32 accumulator with one cast before an fp16 store yields Compiler.assess lowering_eligible=True and a complete CUDA C++ lowering. This is exactly the upstream FIB GEMM shape: C = A @ B.T, FP16 operands, FP16 result. The instruction is tcgen05.mma.cta_group::1.kind::f16, which sm_103a declares and whose _CONTRACT_DTYPES row already admits {BF16, FP16}.

The same retyping on the Triton route is refused twice, each by the rule that owns it: 'triton.dot.fp16_fp32' raises TARGET_INSTRUCTION_UNSUPPORTED because neither sm_100a nor sm_103a declares it, and reusing 'triton.dot.bf16_fp32' for FP16 operands raises MMA_OPERAND_DTYPE_DIFFERS. Neither refusal is a workaround candidate.

WorkloadContract.tensor_abi restates a dtype whitelist {fp32, bf16, int32} instead of quoting the route's own SUPPORTED_DTYPES, so an FP16 tensor cannot be declared by any Workload Contract at all: 'workload tensor x dtype is unsupported'. Both Triton and native_cuda name fp16; the IR's DType names it. This is the shared-layer restatement AGENTS.md calls a defect, and it is the first of the three blockers to hit.

observation: All eight FlashInfer-Bench GEMM captures in flashinfer-bench-tasks (004-011) are FP16 A[M,K] x B[N,K]^T -> C[M,N], and L1_077 is FP16 too. The Compiler is not what blocks them. Three layers above it do, in this order: (1) the Workload ABI cannot name fp16; (2) tasks/devices.py declares no native_cuda backend row, so no task selects the route that does admit the instruction; (3) lab/ has TritonToolchainBuilder, CuTeToolchainBuilder and MetalToolchainBuilder but no native-CUDA ToolchainBuilder, so a native_cuda candidate has no build path. Separately and independently, the Triton route declares no FP16 dot contract on either NVIDIA target, so adding a backend row alone would not serve these tasks on the route the task layer already has. This is the same shape as F-2026-09-15-004: capability that exists at one layer is unreachable because a shared layer restates a set instead of quoting it.
proposed_change: Three separable changes, smallest first. (a) Make WorkloadContract.tensor_abi quote the admitted dtype vocabulary rather than restate it, so a Workload can declare exactly what some route can name; this edits a file pinned by every Executor closure and therefore mints successor Executor Revisions. (b) Declare a native_cuda backend row in tasks/devices.py with its own target, allocation and timing source, or report a measurement-coverage limitation if it cannot state all three. (c) Add a native-CUDA ToolchainBuilder to lab/ so a sealed candidate on that route can be built. Declaring 'triton.dot.fp16_fp32' on an NVIDIA Target is a separate, evidence-gated Target change with its own citation and its own _CONTRACT_DTYPES row (hardware_conformance.py names that site in its own comment); it is not required for (a)-(c) and must not be bundled with them.
